title: Integer `%`: the floor remainder, NULL for a zero divisor
description: `%` on integers is the remainder of floor division, with the sign of the divisor (`-1 % 2` is 1, `1 % -7` is -6). A zero divisor gives NULL, and `MIN % -1` is 0.
reference: `modulus` with `division_type: TRUNCATE` (the remainder has the dividend's sign); `FLOOR` is refused by the model. `on_division_by_zero: ERROR` when omitted. So the reference matches Polars only where the operands have the same sign or the remainder is 0.

provenance.notes: `sverify_dev.probe_polars` runs each expression on edge cases (0, ±1, ±2, 3, ±7, the bounds of the integer width; 0.5, ±2.5, 7, 1e308, ±inf, NaN; NULL), one row at a time, and compares each row with Lean's outcome of the Substrait call under each candidate option (`substrait-check --outcomes`). Observations are Polars programs whose result is recorded as it is. Polars 2.1.0 (Python), Rust crates at tag py-2.1.0 (commit 7f902bd3), on macOS arm64.

evidence.note: `wrapping_floor_div_mod`: `wrapping_div` and `wrapping_rem`, then the divisor is added to a nonzero remainder whose sign differs from it.
Column by column: a zero divisor is masked to NULL.
A literal divisor: 0 gives an all-NULL column, ±1 fills 0, any other a strength-reduced unsigned remainder with the divisor's sign.

notes: Confirms the probes for every width: one macro (`impl_signed_arith_kernel!`) instantiates the kernels for i8, i16, i32, i64 and i128. The remainder is `wrapping_rem` moved into the divisor's sign class, so it is a floor remainder; `MIN % -1` is 0 because `wrapping_rem` gives 0 there (and a literal `-1` divisor fills 0).
Read at tag py-2.1.0 (commit 7f902bd3). The streaming engine evaluates expressions through polars-expr on each morsel (crates/polars-stream/src/expression.rs), so these kernels serve both engines.
